title: tenant-aware-defaults: automated quant + batch/cache preset curator
author: Maya Kline
description:
Motivation: Customers running diverse tenant workloads struggle to pick safe default batching, cache, and quantization profiles. Manual tuning is slow and error-prone, leading to suboptimal unit economics or regressions in tail latency. This PR introduces an automated preset curator that synthesizes tenant-aware defaults from telemetry snapshots and a small rulebook so teams can opt into conservative, balanced, or aggressive presets per tenant.

What this changes: adds a new controller (preset-curator) that consumes workload sketches and generates JSON presets for: batching (max_batch_size, microbatch_target, batch_timeout_ms), KV cache prefill thresholds, and quantization profiles (q8/q4 variants and fallback chains). Presets are exposed via the existing tenant-defaults API and are versioned so rollbacks/rollouts are safe. The curator ships with three starter strategies (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and a dry-run mode which emits telemetry comparing simulated token-cost and 95th latency against current defaults.

Key files touched (high level):
- services/preset-curator/{controller.go,simulator.go,policy_rules.md}
- pkg/telemetry/sketches/{workload_sketch.go,serializer.go}
- api/tenant_defaults/v1/handler.go (adds POST /tenants/:id/presets/dryrun)
- cli/presetctl (new subcommand: apply/dryrun/list)
- integrations/tests/preset-curator-integ.yaml (lightweight scenario harness)

Commits summary:
- 8f9a2dd: scaffold preset-curator service and API hooks
- b2c6f1a: implement workload sketch serializer and stable hashing
- d4e7c3f: add policy rule engine and starter strategies
- e11f9b0: add simulator that replays recent telemetry to estimate unit-econ impact
- f3a12b4: add CLI, docs, and integration test harness

Testing and validation: unit tests for serializer and policy engine, integration harness that simulates three tenant shapes (chatty short prompts, long-form generation, mixed embeddings+chat). Ran a staging dry-run across 50 tenants using one week of telemetry: median token-cost reduction 12% for balanced presets, median 95th latency change +2ms (conservative) and +12ms (aggressive). Dry-run reports included in artifact: ci/preset-curator/dryrun-report-20260228.json.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: presets are additive and opt-in per-tenant. Disabled by default; operations can enable the service per environment. When enabled, default strategy is conservative. Rollout plan: canary 10 tenants -> 100 tenants -> all tenants, monitor unit-econ, errors, tail latency. A built-in safeguard automatically reverts applied presets if error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds for 10 minutes.

Risks and mitigations: automatic quantization can cause rare regressions on small-sample workloads. Mitigation: quant profiles include immediate fallback chains to known-safe FP16/FP32 variants, and the simulator runs classifier heuristics to mark high regression risk tenants.

Related: ENG-8342, ENG-8410, PM-1201.

Release notes: adds tenant-aware preset curator (opt-in) for batching, KV cache, and quantization defaults. CLI support via presetctl. Dry-run mode for safety checks.
